privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.controllerBody: {{org}} runs this playbook and is responsible for the data it holds. If you have a question, write to {{email}} — a real person will read it.
privacy.whatWeProcessLead: We try to store as little as possible. Here's the full list:

wp.admin: Admin email addresses — used to sign you in and to know who invited whom. Passwords go straight to Supabase Auth and are hashed there; we never see them in plain text.
wp.session: A short session cookie (called qm_admin) that just remembers you're signed in. It contains an admin marker and your email — nothing else.
wp.ip: If a sign-in fails, we hold the IP address in memory for 15 minutes so we can slow down brute-force attempts. That's it.
wp.confluence: If you connect a Confluence account, we keep the site name, your Atlassian email, and the access token. The token is encrypted before it touches the database.
wp.content: Whatever admins type into scenarios, categories and tags, and any images they upload. If you're writing about a person, please have a good reason.

privacy.noEmployeeTracking: Employees who just read the playbook don't sign in and aren't tracked. No analytics, no advertising, no third-party scripts.

purpose.admin: So admins can sign in and edit the playbook.
purpose.security: So we can stop someone hammering the sign-in page.
purpose.confluence: So the linked Confluence page shows up inside the scenario for your team.

privacy.legalBasisBody: Legitimate interest for running the playbook and keeping it secure. If you choose to connect Confluence, that's on your consent — disconnect any time from the admin panel.

retention.session: Sign-in cookie: 8 hours or until you log out.
retention.content: Scenario content, categories, and images: until an admin deletes them. Deleting a scenario also deletes its images.
retention.tokens: Confluence tokens: until an admin clicks Disconnect.

sub.supabase: Supabase — hosts the database, image storage, and sign-in. Their DPA: supabase.com/legal/dpa
sub.render: Render — hosts the app itself. Their DPA: render.com/legal/dpa
sub.atlassian: Atlassian — only if an admin connects Confluence. Their DPA: atlassian.com/legal/data-processing-addendum

privacy.transfersBody: We recommend picking EU regions in Supabase and Render (Frankfurt or Ireland) so data stays in the EEA. If it leaves, it does so under the standard EU contract clauses in the DPAs above.
privacy.cookiesBody: One cookie: qm_admin. Only set after you sign in as admin. Employees never get a cookie. We don't use analytics or advertising cookies. Because the one cookie is strictly needed for sign-in, no consent banner is legally required — the small notice at the bottom is just so you know.

sec.https: Everything is served over HTTPS in production, with HSTS on.
sec.encRest: Supabase encrypts the database and file storage at rest.
sec.encTokens: Confluence tokens are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before we store them.
sec.access: Only people on the admin allowlist can sign in. Sign-in uses Supabase Auth, and the session cookie is httpOnly and SameSite=Lax.

rights.access: Ask for a copy of what we hold about you.
rights.rectify: Ask us to correct something wrong.
rights.erase: Ask us to delete data (there may be a legal reason we can't for a while, but we'll tell you).
rights.portability: Ask for the data as a machine-readable JSON file — admins can export directly from the app.
rights.object: Ask us to stop or restrict a specific use of your data.
rights.complain: Complain to your national data-protection authority if we get this wrong.

privacy.contactBody: Email {{email}} for any of these. We'll get back to you within a month, usually much sooner.
privacy.breachBody: If we discover a data breach that could realistically hurt you, we'll tell the supervisory authority within 72 hours and let affected people know without unnecessary delay.

login.title: Admin Portal
login.magicSent: Check your inbox for a sign-in link.
login.resetSent: Check your inbox for a reset link.
login.registerSent: Check your inbox to confirm your address. An admin must invite your email before you can sign in.
login.registerNote: Registering doesn't grant admin access — an existing admin must add your email to the allowlist.
login.exchangeFailed: Could not start a session with the server.
login.supabaseUnavailable: Sign-in service unavailable. Contact an admin.
login.orSupabase: Or sign in with Supabase Auth

reset.title: Set a new password
reset.linkExpired: This reset link has expired or is invalid. Request a new one.
reset.tooShort: Password must be at least 8 characters.
reset.success: Password updated. Sign in with your new password.

admins.title: Manage Admins
admins.help: Add or remove people who can sign in as admin. New rows do not create a Supabase account — the invited person still has to register or sign in with the same email. Revoking keeps the row for audit and flips their access off.
admins.emptyList: No admins yet. Invite someone above.
admins.inviteSent: Invitation email sent to {{email}}. They'll set a password via the link.
admins.inviteExisting: {{email}} already has an account. We sent a sign-in link so they know they've been granted access.
admins.inviteEmailFailed: {{email}} was added to the allowlist, but the email couldn't be sent: {{reason}}. Ask them to sign up manually — the account will work once they do.

cookie.body: We only set one cookie — for admin sign-in. Employees don't get any cookies. No tracking, no ads.

categories.title: Manage Categories
categories.help: Categories appear in employee filters and the scenario form. Delete is blocked while scenarios use a category.
categories.label: Label
categories.empty: No categories yet. Add the first one above.

scenarioForm.title: Title
scenarioForm.needOneLanguage: Fill in the title, scenario, and solution for at least one language.
scenarioForm.partialWarn: Some languages have only partial content and won't be shown to employees ({{langs}}). Save anyway?
scenarioForm.unsavedConfirm: You have unsaved changes. Discard them?
scenarioForm.languagesHelp: Fill in one, two, or all three. Employees see the version that matches their UI language, or the first one available.

confluence.title: Confluence Integration
confluence.help: Link a Confluence page to a scenario and employees will see its content on the scenario page. The token is stored server-side, encrypted, and never leaves the API.
confluence.loadFailed: Could not load the Confluence page.
confluence.notConnectedHint: Connect a Confluence account below. Only admins can do this.
confluence.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect Confluence? Linked pages will stop rendering until you reconnect.
confluence.cloudBlurb: Sign in with your own Atlassian account. You'll be redirected to Atlassian and back. The refresh token is encrypted before it's stored.
confluence.cloudNotConfigured: Cloud OAuth isn't configured on the server. Set CONFLUENCE_CLIENT_ID, CONFLUENCE_CLIENT_SECRET, and CONFLUENCE_REDIRECT_URI.
confluence.dcBlurb: Paste your Confluence base URL and a Personal Access Token (Profile → Personal Access Tokens in Confluence).
confluence.patStorageNote: The PAT is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM). It is never returned to the browser.
confluence.dcNeedFields: Base URL and PAT are required.
confluence.pickerNoConnection: Connect Confluence from the sidebar to link a page.
